papers.title: Managing unreliable suppliers under varying risk preferences: all-or-nothing versus fractional delivery guarantees
papers.authors: Yasemin Merzifonluoglu, Ismail Serdar Bakal, Marie Versteeg & Arnout den Hollander
papers.idea: Studies the newsvendor problem with all-or-nothing and fractional-delivery-guarantee suppliers. In the risk-neutral setting, suppliers are activated in increasing unit procurement cost, while disruption parameters influence order sizes and activation thresholds. It also compares variance and weighted-variance measures of profit risk.
papers.relevance: The core research article for the Decision Making Under Uncertainty assignment: supplier selection, delivery disruptions and risk preferences underpin the optimization and simulation models being studied.

papers.title: A Reality Check for Data Snooping
papers.blurb: Testing the best result from a specification search against a benchmark, using a bootstrap that accounts for data reuse.
papers.idea: Develops a bootstrap-based Reality Check for the joint null that no candidate forecast or trading rule is superior to a benchmark after a specification search.
papers.relevance: A statistical check on apparent improvements that may have been found only because many models were tried.

papers.title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
papers.authors: David H. Bailey, Jonathan M. Borwein, Marcos López de Prado & Qiji Jim Zhu
papers.journal: Working-paper revision (later published in the Journal of Computational Finance)
papers.blurb: Using combinatorially symmetric cross-validation to estimate how often the in-sample winner falls below the median out of sample.
papers.idea: Formalizes the Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO) and estimates it with combinatorially symmetric cross-validation (CSCV), using in-sample and out-of-sample rankings of strategy trials.
papers.relevance: A way to assess whether the process of choosing a best-performing backtest tends to select noise.

papers.title: Large Sample Properties of Generalized Method of Moments Estimators
papers.idea: Generalized method of moments estimates parameters using sample moment restrictions and establishes large-sample properties under stated assumptions.
papers.relevance: Provides the theoretical basis for two-step GMM and Hansen J-tests used to evaluate the CAPM stochastic discount factor.

papers.title: A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix
papers.authors: Whitney K. Newey & Kenneth D. West
papers.idea: Develops a covariance-matrix estimator for heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation in time-series settings under suitable conditions.
papers.relevance: Clarifies why conventional OLS inference can be misleading for financial returns and how HAC errors change alpha tests.

papers.title: A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model
papers.authors: Eugene F. Fama & Kenneth R. French
papers.idea: Extends factor asset pricing to include profitability and investment alongside market, size and value factors.
papers.relevance: Provides the five-factor benchmark compared with CAPM and clarifies why stronger regression fit need not mean smaller pricing errors.

papers.title: On Persistence in Mutual Fund Performance
papers.idea: Uses a momentum factor with market, size and value factors to study patterns in mutual fund performance.
papers.relevance: Motivates examining momentum as a missing dimension in models that otherwise explain significant return variation.

papers.title: Some Tests of Specification for Panel Data: Monte Carlo Evidence and an Application to Employment Equations
papers.idea: Studies dynamic panel GMM specification tests, including serial-correlation checks and tests of overidentifying restrictions.
papers.relevance: Connects panel instruments and moment restrictions to the principles of consistent GMM estimation.

papers.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality
papers.authors: David H. Bailey & Marcos López de Prado
papers.idea: Introduces the Deflated Sharpe Ratio, adjusting Sharpe-ratio significance for multiple strategy trials and non-normal returns.
papers.relevance: Helps examine whether a high reported Sharpe ratio still looks compelling after allowing for selection bias, sample length, skewness and kurtosis.
